paragraphs.text: Loch Prith is an underground lake on Cridhe located through a secret entrance of the Westlands.

Even after the Parting , Loch Prith kept its natural beauty, with several chambers of abundant wildlife, butterflies, lumini, elves , and other refugees of Inys Nohr . It was always both day and night in the settlement, and fruits were never out of season. Its chambers include the hall of the orbs , which contains the lumini and food crops, the orchid chamber , the prophetess’s receiving hall , the Gwylfan's grotto , and the hives , which hold those gripped by sickness.

Loch Prith was ruled by its original inhabitants, the three Gwylfan Antistita , Vestira , and Praetis , also called the World Weavers. It was said that the Gwylfan were placed at Loch Prith by the Maker when the world was very young. The Gwylfan wove the story of Cridhe's history, the words of the Maker, and prophecies of its future, on a large loom of red rosewood, hanging the tapestries in the halls of Loch Prith. After speaking with them, a visitor could ask a single question.

After spending centuries at the court of Inys Nohr following her own prophetic visions, Thrissa returned to Loch Prith after giving birth to Nazir . Almost 30 years later, her husband Feryar arrived with Aylith of Inys Haen , a girl they called the Mender. Aylith went through several trials in the caves of Loch Prith - first, she was healed of her mortal wounds by the elven herbs and magic. Then Aylith met with the Gwylfan, who told her more of her destiny, setting up her further trials. Aylith traveled into the darkness inside her and freed herself from it, though she did not manage to destroy it utterly. Her next task was then to leave Loch Prith, and on the way, she faced Raphos the blacksmith, who had become frozen at the time of his impending death. He almost killed her, but when he touched her flesh, he was healed of his hatred, and disintegrated. After the Mending of the Clan Tree , Feryar offered Loch Prith as a home to the Mirkalbions, where they could stay and grow abundant ardré away from the bright world above.
